title: The panel comes back in the same frame as the selection it describes
goal: Clicking a layer after nothing was selected is the slowest click there is: the whole right hand panel has to be built from nothing, nine sliders, text fields and a colour well, and the click waits for all of it. The picture should react at once and the panel should catch up, so a click never feels like it is thinking.
notes: Follow-up from the selection latency work merged 2026-09-04, which took the common click from 63ms of main thread work to 46ms but left this one at a 53ms run loop pass. Cause is section creation: Position and Size, Effects, Shadow and Component all mount at once. Two options the runner should weigh and record: keep those sections mounted and hidden, or hand the dock its update one run loop pass after the canvas so handles land first. Measure with Scripts/playtest/select-click-perf-walk.json, which reports mainBusy and the longest pass per click.
acceptance: Measured with the selection walk: the click that brings the panel back after a deselect costs no more than a click that only moves the selection
The canvas handles and highlight appear in the first frame after the click, before the panel finishes
No section flickers or jumps as it arrives, and nothing is left blank once the panel settles
Numbers before and after are in the audit under queue/audits/, taken with the same walk

log.note: Adversarial review before building. Option A from the notes (keep the sections mounted and hidden) was rejected on UX grounds, not perf: Position & Size, Effects and Shadow standing over nothing is a panel describing something that is not there, which the user has already reported once, and it moves the build cost onto every click instead of one. Option B (hand the dock its new sections one run-loop pass after the canvas) is the shortest version that delivers the value, so that is what was built. Departures are deliberately NOT deferred: a Shadow section left standing over an empty selection for a frame is worse than a briefly shorter panel.

Baseline on the probe with Scripts/playtest/select-click-perf-walk.json. Come-back click (300,270) after a deselect: mainBusy 85.8/85.2/91.1ms, longest pass 62.9/59.7/65.9ms, 3 passes. A click that only moves the selection (950,520): mainBusy 60.3/57.0/61.6ms, longest 44.3/42.3/45.3ms. Dock goes from 2 sections (Layers, Library) to 7, so five sections mount inside the click.

Built: PhotonzCore/PanelSectionArrival.swift (pure, 10 tests) decides what the dock may draw this pass; DockArrivals in LayersPanel.swift keeps the bookkeeping outside observed state so recording it costs no re-draw; InspectorPanel draws PanelSectionArrival.showing(...) and bumps a @State counter one main-queue hop later to draw the pass that mounts what it held back. A click that keeps the same section list never reaches any of it.

After, same walk: come-back click mainBusy 87.5/89.0/66.4ms, longest pass 44.5/43.9/42.9ms over 6/6/4 passes. Move-selection click unchanged at longest 43.9/43.7/45.4ms. So the frame-dropping pass is now identical between the two clicks; total main-thread time is unchanged because the five sections still genuinely cost about 22ms to build, they just build after the canvas has drawn.

Acceptance, honestly: (1) met on the longest run-loop pass, which is the frame that gets dropped, NOT met on total main-thread time; the audit says so in plain words. (2) partly: the handles land about 20ms earlier and before the panel finishes, but not inside one frame, because the click's own pass still re-runs the whole dock for the Layers list, which is the already-queued task a-layers-list-with-many-rows-costs-no-more-per-c. (3) verified with a second walk: no animation on the section set, so nothing slides or jumps, and the dock settles at Layers, Position & Size, Layout, Effects, Shadow, Library with every field filled (screenshot in the audit). (4) numbers before and after are in queue/audits/2026-09-04-panel-arrival.json.

InspectorPanel is shared between Current and Next rather than forked. This is scheduling, not behavior, and forking the whole dock to change when a section mounts would be a large duplication for no visible difference; the same shared files were changed by the selection latency work on 2026-09-04. Both releases get it.
